chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Big bands after Glenn Miller: Kenton and the later leaders
summary: Wilson says Kenton was the last big new idea, while later bands like Mel Lewis, Maynard Ferguson and Buddy Rich are not carrying it forward.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Because it had gotten kind of stagnant there, and when Glenn Miller came up and he began to add beautiful tone colors in his band and the cute stuff, you know, novelties like 'The Kalamazoo' and the 'Chatanooga Choo Choo' and 'Pennsylvania 6,5000' -- all that good kind of music along with straight jazz, and then the other bands were getting a little stale, nobody was thinking too much of new ideas until Kenton came up - and that was maybe the last really valid new idea that had a big public, and fine musicians, all combined together, the Kenton band.

Because after that, the next new bands -- the Buddy Morrows and the -- they were rehashes of --tried to carry on-- the, drained the money out of the Glenn Miller ideas, getting different guys to front there, the Tommy Dorsey band conducted by Lee Castle, you know, the Jimmy Dorsey band led by this and the other -- there hasn't been really a big new jazz band
Yeah. Well, Kenton would be the more dominant force, with more impact on the world of big band jazz music.
Until the next thing after that would be, or might have been would be the Mel Lewis big band, right?
The most important one after Kenton?

Yeah, uh huh. And of course, the Buddy Rich big band now is excellent. But somehow or other, I feel that these bands are not exactly on the right track to carry the thing forward from where Kenton was at.
